## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment-variable default, because the project's CLI flag rules require one for every new flag. The exclusion logic itself is covered by the added unit and end-to-end tests.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect()` now skips files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped path. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests and adds a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default --exclude from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE env var — `--exclude` is a new flag under `cli/`, but it uses `default=[]` and never reads `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`. That breaks `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable … because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot set exclusions, so excluded files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Read `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` into the default, choose and document how it separates multiple patterns, add the variable to `docs/flags.md:7`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-set case.
